bottleneck: In 'partial-observation-backtrack' and its mirror, the agent stood on a cell with known, unvisited neighbors (tiles at (1,2)/(2,1) and (2,2)/(1,1)) yet kept speculating out-of-graph left moves, producing 3 'destination is not walkable' blocks, 0 waits, and score 0 in 4 steps; the prior candidate (ex-partial-frontier-neighbor-01) used width/height-bound speculation even when a known frontier transition existed.
rationale: Treat observation.tiles as the known graph and act on it only: if a known neighbor of the agent's cell exists, prefer an unvisited known neighbor (frontier expansion), otherwise backtrack through the least-visited known neighbor (visit counts derived from context.memory action positions plus accepted move destinations). Speculate within width/height bounds only when no known neighbor exists yet, and never retry a direction from a position where context.memory records accepted=false for that exact move. Direction is chosen purely from observed data, so mirrored holdouts behave symmetrically. Returns undefined (defer to baseline) whenever parcels/keys/doors/batteries are visible, energy is zero, or the observation is malformed, protecting the key-door, battery, and delivery holdouts.
expectedMetric: partial-observation-backtrack and partial-observation-backtrack-mirror: achieved=true, score >= 8, 0 'destination is not walkable' blocks (was 3 blocks, score 0 in 4 steps); partial-observation-frontier and frontier-mirror stay achieved at score 8; key-door-delivery (10), battery-return (10), simple-delivery (5), two-parcels (13), detour-delivery (10) unchanged via deferral.
